ai.description: This lizard reaches 20–25 cm. It features a mottled brown and green body with a distinct white or yellow stripe along the flanks and a prominent nuchal crest. Males possess a bright red throat patch.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Japalura variegata* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, enlarged, white or pale-colored scale patch located just above the tympanum.
ai.habitat: *Japalura variegata* inhabits temperate broadleaf and coniferous forests in the Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 3,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Variegated Mountain Lizard is primarily diurnal, often remaining motionless on tree trunks to ambush passing insects while relying on its cryptic coloration for defense.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Japalura variegata* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 4–8 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between May and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Japalura variegata* is found in the Eastern Himalayas, specifically across Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, and West Bengal, at elevations between 1,000 and 2,500 meters.
